newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden sees further fall in long debt yields.
newsitem.headline: Sweden sees further fall in long debt yields.

text.p: The Swedish government said on Friday it believed long interest rates could further a decline embarked upon in April 1995.

"The government is of the opinion that long interest rates may continue to fall further since inflation and state finances are in firm control," Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said in the government's 1997 budget.

In a no-surprises budget document, Asbrink said international confidence in the Swedish economy had increased, noting that long yields (the five-year government bond) had fallen to around seven percent from 11 percent in April 1995.
"Lower inflation and increased confidence has enabled the Riksbank (central bank) to ease monetary policy and cut the repo rate on a number of occasions in 1996," Asbrink noted.
The repo rate, which is the central bank's key monetary policy tool, has been reduced to 5.15 percent from the level of 8.91 percent at which it started the year.
